svg.aria-label: Customer-owned MCP Hub as the tool backend
svg.title: Customer-owned MCP Hub as the tool backend
svg.text: Customer-owned MCP Hub as the tool backend

One hub serves production and development · every request is HMAC-signed per application (MCPHUB-HMAC-SHA256) · permissions follow the forwarded SSO token, which the platform cannot swap (its hash is inside the signature)
demo: EC2 in the platform VPC · production: your network, reachable from the runtime

Two signatures, one permission model: the HMAC names the application — each published agent signs with its own key pair; everything pre-publish signs as the shared dev-workbench pair, which the hub can rate-limit or revoke on its own.

The SSO token names the user and rides untouched from the caller to your backends; the hub picks each caller's tools from its department claim — the demo app is sales, alice is hr, so the same attachment shows different tools.
actor key pairs · read by secret name
app token 8 h · user token 1 h
